cases.label: Champion Smite Armour Stacker
cases.notes: The source documents armour ranging into the millions and explicitly calls out degen/recovery as a weakness despite huge headline armour and hit mitigation.

cases.label: Int/Accuracy Stacking Juggernaut
cases.notes: The source documents Intelligence feeding accuracy/evasion/ES and enabling additional attack-speed/damage scaling; the attack skill is comparatively flexible because the scaling engine lives elsewhere.

cases.label: Cast on Ward Break Reliquarian trigger loop
cases.notes: Ward is both a defensive state and a trigger-rate resource. Eye of Innocence self-damage breaks Ward; frequent hit skills help restore it. More Ward above the documented trigger CDR cap is not automatically an offensive upgrade.

cases.label: Flamewood Rejuvenation Totem Chieftain
cases.notes: The guide explicitly says single-target improves when bosses attack frequently. Less-recovery/no-regen map conditions can change RF viability, so content state is part of build viability.

cases.label: Shield Crush Juggernaut final-form armour transition
cases.notes: Shield defence is an offensive input. Late progression adds Replica Dreamfeather armour scaling and 90% maximum elemental resistance; gear order matters because some pieces depend on others to avoid survivability regressions.

cases.label: 3.28 Mana Stacker Archmage to crit Spark transition
cases.notes: Historical example of a deliberately delayed endgame skill transition: the guide builds the mana/Archmage foundation first and swaps to crit Spark only when gear can support the archetype.

assertions.summary: Very high armour does not make an armour stacker universally safe: the reviewed 3.29 sources still identify recovery/degen and very large single-hit failure modes, so diagnosis must preserve damage type, recovery and hit-size context.

In the reviewed Int/Accuracy Juggernaut, Intelligence participates in several systems at once through enabling items: accuracy, attack scaling, ES and evasion. Evaluating an Intelligence roll as a single generic attribute bonus would miss most of its build value.

The reviewed Cast on Ward Break setup treats Ward as a trigger-rate resource with a documented cooldown-recovery cap. Once the cap is reached, additional Ward is not automatically an offensive upgrade, making explicit breakpoint detection mandatory.

Flamewood Totem practical single-target depends materially on enemy hit frequency against the totems. Encounter behaviour therefore changes effective damage delivery even when the character sheet and PoB configuration are unchanged.

The reviewed Shield Crush progression documents dependencies where changing one item before its enabling counterpart can reduce or break survivability. Upgrade solving must validate coordinated transition packages, not assume every individually stronger-looking item is safe to equip immediately.

A historical endgame archetype may intentionally level and map with a different skill/scaling package until the final build has enough gear to function. Build understanding must model transition prerequisites rather than judging an earlier stage against the final skill in isolation.
